subject: Re: Defining 'Customer Data' vs. 'Derived Models' — DPA redlines and signing plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@finovate.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Finovate Procurement <procurement@finovate.com>, Finovate Security <security@finovate.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Customer Data definition and ML-use exclusions (DPA)

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for sending the initial DPA. Before we move to signature, our legal and security teams want to confirm a couple of carve-outs around model training and the subprocessor list:

1) We need an explicit prohibition on training models using "Customer Confidential Data" (examples: PII, contracts, health records). We can allow aggregate, anonymized telemetry for service quality but not training that could reproduce customer content.
2) Please provide an up-to-date subprocessor matrix (company, region, function) and confirm any planned changes in the next 90 days.
3) Cross-border transfer protections — confirm KMS/HSM and export controls for EU data.

Can you propose final language for the DPA so procurement can review it and we can sign via DocuSign? We are targeting signature by the week of Dec 13.

Attachments: none from our side.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Legal Ops, Finovate, Inc.
Procurement: procurement@finovate.com
Security: security@finovate.com

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena@finovate.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Customer Data definition and ML-use exclusions (DPA)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. Summary of Redwood's proposed approach below; attached are the redlines and a current subprocessor CSV for your review.

- Definitions: We propose to split "Customer Data" into two buckets in the DPA: 
  * "Customer Content" — raw content uploaded or submitted by the customer (documents, messages, files).
  * "Customer Metadata" — usage metadata, request timing, system logs.

- Training prohibition: Redwood will NOT use Customer Content or Data that is reasonably identifiable to a customer for training or model improvement. We propose the clause: "Provider shall not use Customer Content or any data reasonably identifiable to Customer to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider models for use with third-party customers."

- Allowed telemetry: aggregate, de-identified telemetry and performance metrics may be used to improve system reliability and capacity planning. We include a requirement to publish an annual telemetry summary and maintain a mechanism for customers to opt out of non-essential telemetry.

- Model derivatives: we accept that models may generate outputs derived from processing Customer Content for the customer's use, but such derivatives will not be fed back into training datasets without express consent.

- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors (compute, monitoring, logging, analytics). We commit to 30-day notice for new subprocessors and to provide a point-in-time export if you need a security review.

- Cross-border: confirm support for regional data residency and KMS integration; we'll propose standard export control language and HSM/KMS references in the transfers section.

Next steps: Marissa, could you and Neha take a pass on tightening the training-prohibition language and add execution instructions for DocuSign? Marissa, please also confirm whether the SOC 2 summary is the right artifact for Finovate's security team.

Attachments: redlines_tessa_v1.docx (proposed DPA redlines), subprocessor_matrix_20261202.csv

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Legal, Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0142

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Elena Park <elena@finovate.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Customer Data definition and ML-use exclusions (DPA)

Morning — quick clarification from Legal: we need to be explicit about what we mean by 'model derivatives' so there is no ambiguity that derived outputs generated for the customer are permitted to be returned to that customer, but those outputs cannot be retained in training corpora. Suggest the following sentence for insertion: "Derived Outputs produced solely in response to Customer Content for the Customer's exclusive use shall remain Customer Content for the purposes of this Agreement; Provider will not use such Derived Outputs to train Provider models without Customer's separate written consent."

Also adding a short DocuSign execution block: once redlines are agreed, Redwood will upload the final DPA to DocuSign and add procurement@finovate.com as the primary signer. We will include a final checklist (subprocessor CSV, SOC 2 summary, KMS config) as attachments in the DocuSign envelope.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:38:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Customer Data definition and ML-use exclusions (DPA)

Adding security notes from our side:

- SOC 2: attached is a high-level SOC 2 summary (SOC2_summary_redwood_dec2026.pdf). We are completing the full audit report this quarter and can provide a redacted copy under NDA if needed.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM workflows for private deployments. We will add explicit language to the transfers section referencing CMEK and bring-your-own-key for private instances.
- Subprocessor governance: we honor 30-day notice and offer a 14-day escalation window for any subprocessor that would handle PII.
- Cross-border: propose standard SCCs and a data processing addendum for EU customers; for Finovate (US headquartered) we will call out region controls for any EU-origin data.

Attachment: SOC2_summary_redwood_dec2026.pdf

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Tessa / team —

Thank you, this is helpful. Procurement and security reviewed your proposed language and we have two small asks before we can approve: 

1) Please add an explicit opt-out mechanism for customers to prevent even de-identified telemetry from being used for system improvement (some of our regulated lines prefer a stricter posture).
2) Confirm the cadence and format of the subprocessor notice (CSV + bulletin email is fine). We also need a signed statement that there are no planned subprocessor changes in the next 30 days.

If you can update the redlines with the opt-out mechanism and provide the signed statement, we are happy to proceed to DocuSign. Target: signature by Dec 15.

Once signed, procurement will route payment and our CS team will coordinate go-live.

Elena Park
